ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $CE$ is the angle bisector of the exterior angle $\angle ACD$ of $\triangle ABC$, and $CE$ intersects the extension of $BA$ at point $E$. If $\angle B=35^\circ$ and $\angle E=25^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CAE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle DCE$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle BCE$ and $\angle B=35^\circ$, $\angle E=25^\circ$,
\[\therefore \angle DCE=\angle B+\angle E=60^\circ,\]
Since $CE$ bisects $\angle ACD$,
\[\therefore \angle ACE=\angle DCE=60^\circ,\]
\[\therefore \angle CAE=180^\circ-\angle ACE-\angle E=\boxed{95^\circ}.\]
